title: Client-side rate adaptive backoff scratchpad
body:
Purpose:
Quick personal notes + draft spec for a small client-side rate-adaptive backoff/governor that we can ship as a lightweight SDK helper. Target: reduce cold spikes to hosted API and avoid hammering Dedicated endpoints during transient errors or throttles. Mostly thinking about heuristics, observable signals, and an open-but-constrained config shape to expose to apps.

Goals:
- Prevent cascade retries from many clients after transient outage (thundering herd).
- Smooth token/req throughput to match configured SLOs per route.
- Adapt to server-side Retry-After, 429s, 5xx, and network flakiness.
- Be conservative by default but tunable by product teams.
- Provide telemetry hooks (counters/histograms) for ops to diagnose.

Non-goals:
- Not a substitute for server-side rate limiting or quota enforcement.
- Not intended to be a full circuit-breaker library (but should interop).

Constraints/assumptions:
- Clients are mobile/web/server SDKs with intermittent connectivity.
- A single process (or browser tab) runs one governor instance per tenant/token.
- Config should be serializable (JSON) and small.
- Must not block developer code paths: non-blocking timers and async.

High-level design notes (sketch):
1) Signals considered:
   - successful requests / latencies (p50/p95)
   - 429s with optional Retry-After header
   - 503/502/5xx counts
   - network timeouts / DNS failures
   - local concurrency (in-flight requests)
2) Goals for outputs:
   - PER-REQUEST decision: allow | delay (ms) | reject-with-error
   - suggested backoff delta for caller to apply when doing retries
   - expose current "rate-credit" token bucket value for telemetry
3) Runtime model:
   - token-bucket style credit that refills at configurable rate R (requests/sec equivalent)
   - when encountering server-suggested Retry-After, consume extra credits and lower refill rate temporarily
   - an additive slow-start when app starts (avoid immediate full-rate burst)
   - fast recovery window for isolated network hiccups, slower after sustained 5xxs

API/config shape (draft, small):
{
  "governor_version": "1",
  "initial_rate_per_min": 60,           // conservative default
  "max_burst": 10,                     // allow short bursts
  "slow_start_window_s": 30,           // ramp up at startup
  "penalty_multiplier": 0.5,           // multiply refill rate on penalty
  "penalty_decay_s": 300,              // how long penalty fades to zero (seconds)
  "retry_after_behavior": "aggressive", // aggressive | moderate | conservative
  "max_concurrent": 8,                 // local concurrency cap
  "telemetry_labels": ["route", "tenant"],
  "sampling": { "success_rate": 0.1, "error_rate": 1.0 }
}

Notes on fields:
- initial_rate_per_min: initial refill. client can override based on environment (mobile=lower).
- max_burst: how many tokens can be spent immediately when bucket is full.
- penalty_multiplier: when we see sustained 5xx or many 429s, multiply refill by this factor (<1 reduces rate).
- retry_after_behavior: influences how we parse Retry-After (seconds vs HTTP-date) and whether to apply hard pause.

Example pseudocode (behavioral):
// on each request wantToSend():
- now = now()
- refillTokens(now)
- if inHardPause(now): return { decision: "reject", reason: "retry-after" }
- if tokens >= 1 and inFlight < max_concurrent: tokens -= 1; inFlight++; return { decision: "allow" }
- else: computeDelay = backoffForState(); schedule attempt after computeDelay; return { decision: "delay", delayMs: computeDelay }

// on response handleResponse(resp):
- inFlight--
- if resp.status == 200: observeSuccessLatency(resp.latency)
- if resp.status == 429: handle429(resp)
- if resp.status in [500,502,503,504]: handleServerError(resp)
- handleNetworkError() for timeouts etc.

handle429(resp):
- if resp.headers.Retry-After exists: setHardPause(until=parsedHeader)
- increment consecutive429s counter
- applyPenaltyFactor()

applyPenaltyFactor():
- current_refill_rate *= penalty_multiplier
- penalty_expiry = now + penalty_decay_s
- emitTelemetry("penalty_applied")

RefillTokens(now):
- delta = now - last_refill_time
- tokens += delta * refill_rate
- tokens = min(tokens, max_burst)
- last_refill_time = now

Backoff policy (heuristic):
- Short delays (50-200ms) for local concurrency stalls (smooth client-side queuing)
- Exponential-ish backoff for repeated 429/5xx: base = 200ms, multiply by 1.5–2.0 per consecutive error up to cap (5–10s)
- If Retry-After specified, prefer server instruction (capped at config max, e.g. 60s)

Sequence diagram (text):
Client SDK -> Governor: wantToSend(request)
Governor -> Client SDK: allow/delay/reject
Client SDK -> Server: request (if allow)
Server -> Client SDK: 200|429|5xx
Client SDK -> Governor: handleResponse(resp)

Telemetry (must have):
- gauge: governor.current_tokens
- counter: governor.penalty_applied_total
- counter: governor.requests_allowed_total
- counter: governor.requests_delayed_total
- histogram: governor.delay_ms
- tags: route, tenant, region

Rollout plan (quick):
- experiment in hosted SDK: default off for first month. Enable for 5% of SDK users keyed by tenant hash.
- collect telemetry for 2 weeks, flag where server-side 429s drop then tune defaults.
- iterate: try conservative vs moderate retry-after behavior per-route.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How much should client infer global rate vs respecting server-side quotas? If servers report bucket/credits, should client sync? (prefer: yes if available, but rare).
- TTL and storage: should token bucket be persisted across app restarts? (mobile: helpful; risk: stale state).
- DOS vector: malicious clients could set extremely high initial_rate; need SDK-enforced max caps (config + baked-in hard caps).
- UX: when we delay, do apps expect a retry promise or an immediate error? Default: delay with promise; allow opt-out immediate-fail mode.

TODOs (personal):
- [ ] spin up small sim to model 1000 clients ramping with N% error inject; tune penalty_multiplier and decay.
- [ ] wire basic telemetry to hosted-dev and run smoke test
- [ ] draft a short SDK README + example usage
- [ ] ask infra if servers could return a small JSON payload with "client_readable_quota" in 429 (design API?)
- [ ] write unit tests for concurrency edge cases (race between refill & response)

Notes-to-self (random):
- Keep API tiny: most users only need initial_rate_per_min and max_concurrent; others are knobs for power users.
- Consider metric: fraction of requests delayed vs allowed as health signal for route saturation.
- For Dedicated customers: expose server-coordinated tokens via telemetry channel in future.

End of scratchpad.
